title: Reporting of RNA-guided Cas9 DNA cutting (CRISPR gene editing)
summary: In June 2012 a team that included Jennifer Doudna and Emmanuelle Charpentier reported that a two-RNA complex from bacterial immunity could guide the Cas9 enzyme to cut DNA at chosen sites. The announcing university release said the system offered a straightforward way to cleave any desired site in a genome. Doudna said genome editing had not yet been demonstrated, but that it was now a very real possibility.

uncertainty.note: Online publication date from the HHMI page; ScienceDaily reprint is dated June 28, 2012.

as_recorded.value: In a paper published online June 28, 2012, in the journal Science

where.modern_name: Berkeley, California, United States (PROXY PIN: University of California, Berkeley, where Jennifer Doudna's group was based; the research was international)
where.historical_name: Berkeley, California, United States; no polity at this date. Proxy pin for a study by collaborators in Berkeley and Umeå, Sweden

importance.justification: The sources describe a programmable RNA-guided system that can cut DNA at any chosen site, which the authors said could be used for genome editing, a very real possibility per Doudna.
